title: Wittmann holds off Rast in Brands Hatch Race 1 after Di Resta leads for Aston Martin
dek: Marco Wittmann won DTM Race 1 at Brands Hatch for BMW from pole by 0.374 seconds from René Rast, after Paul di Resta’s Aston Martin led the first 14 laps.

chapters.title: A home round for Aston Martin with the title still open
text: The DTM reached Brands Hatch on 10–11 August for the sixth of nine rounds, with René Rast of Audi Sport Team Rosberg leading the championship, Abt Sportsline’s Nico Müller second and BMW’s Marco Wittmann third. The first ten races had produced six different winners: Rast and Wittmann had three victories each, with single wins for Philipp Eng, Müller, Bruno Spengler and Mike Rockenfeller.

It was also the first time R-Motorsport’s Aston Martin Vantage DTM, in its first season in the series, raced on home soil. Its line-up included Paul di Resta and Jake Dennis. The round used the full Grand Prix circuit.

The format was the familiar one: two races of 55 minutes plus one lap, one mandatory four-tyre stop, no refuelling and Hankook control tyres. Qualifying took place on the morning of each race, so Saturday’s grid was set only a few hours before the start, in weather that kept changing.

chapters.title: A red flag, an Aston on slicks and Wittmann’s pole at the death
text: Saturday’s qualifying was played out in changeable conditions. Spengler completed a single lap on wet tyres before switching, and Philipp Eng, still on wets, set provisional pole. Then Pietro Fittipaldi lost control of his WRT Audi at Paddock Hill Bend and slid backwards into the tyre barrier, tearing off the rear of the car and the left-hand door. The session was red-flagged for a long spell, and WRT team-mate Jonathan Aberdein had an off as it was stopped.

When it resumed, Dennis took the Aston Martin out on slick tyres and went provisional pole with 1m16.342s, almost two seconds clear of the field at that point. The rest took until the closing minutes to respond. Rast went to the top with 1m15.723s, but in the final seconds Wittmann crossed the line with a 1m15.654s, 0.069 seconds faster, to take pole for BMW Team RMG.

Loïc Duval was third on 1m16.012s and di Resta’s Vantage fourth on 1m16.067s after two quick late laps, which was R-Motorsport’s second-best qualifying of its debut season. Robin Frijns, Sheldon van der Linde and Dennis followed, with Müller eighth and Timo Glock ninth after a high-speed off at Paddock Hill Bend in the opening minutes. Daniel Juncadella was tenth, so three Astons were in the top ten. Eng and Rockenfeller were 11th and 12th, Green 13th after leading the session at one stage, and Ferdinand Habsburg 15th after an earlier practice off at Druids. Fittipaldi’s repaired car could not be ready in time, and he did not start.

After the session the DTM confirmed that BMW had asked for the seals to be opened on three additional engines. Under the rules, that meant the three best-placed BMW drivers in the race would not score for BMW in the manufacturers’ classification.

chapters.title: Di Resta jumps from fourth to the lead
text: The track was dry enough for slicks, though rain threatened throughout. Wittmann and Rast both bogged down, while Di Resta made a getaway so quick that it was later ruled a jump start. He swept around the outside of Wittmann into Paddock Hill Bend and led, and Duval also passed Rast for third. By the end of the first lap Di Resta was almost a second clear, and his defensive driving kept the Vantage in front through the opening phase.

There was damage behind. Juncadella’s fast start pushed Glock’s BMW into the Aston of Dennis, whose rear wing was damaged, and he was out on the first lap. For Di Resta, the stewards’ video showed the Aston rolling slightly just before the lights went out, and he was given a five-second penalty to serve at his stop. DTM boss Gerhard Berger said the start was measured by a sensor and was on the limit.

chapters.title: Wittmann gets the undercut and slips through at Paddock Hill Bend
text: With rain still threatening, nobody stopped very early, and the leaders came in from around the middle of the race. Wittmann came in on lap 14, two laps before Di Resta, and Rast and Duval followed him. The pivotal moment came at Paddock Hill Bend, where Green, having pitted early, ran wide while the leaders came together on their cold tyres. Wittmann steered through the gap that opened up and passed Rast, who had been the net leader.

Di Resta pitted on lap 16 and had to stop first at the stewards’ box to serve his five seconds before the crew changed his four tyres, which dropped him down the order. Once the stops had shaken out Wittmann led Rast by more than five seconds, with Müller close behind the second Audi. Frijns, Eng and Spengler were among those who stayed out longest, and Frijns was the last to change tyres, on lap 24. By lap 25 the whole field had completed its mandatory stop.

chapters.title: Wittmann’s tyres fade, Rast runs out of laps
text: Wittmann’s tyres dropped away in the closing stages, and a slow lap let Rast close from more than five seconds to within three. The Audi driver loomed in his mirrors on the last lap, but could not find a way past, and Wittmann took the flag 0.374 seconds clear for his fourth win of the season. Müller finished third, 8.566 seconds behind, after Rast had moved past him and Duval following the stops.

Frijns, on the freshest tyres, took Rockenfeller and Duval to finish fourth, and Duval held fifth from Eng, who passed Rockenfeller for sixth on lap 38 but could not get by the Frenchman. Rockenfeller was seventh and van der Linde eighth. Aberdein was ninth and Juncadella tenth, the best of the Astons. Di Resta had been running eighth with five minutes to go when a mechanical problem stopped him in the closing laps, and he was classified 14th, three laps down. Habsburg was classified 15th, four laps behind.

Rast still led the championship on 178 points. Wittmann said afterwards he was happy that “Aston Martin was leading a race” at their home round, while Di Resta insisted his start had been no more than what drivers had done for years.

facts.t: Wittmann’s fourth win of the year
facts.v: Wittmann won Race 1 by 0.374 seconds from Rast, with Müller third, as tyre wear almost caught him on the final laps.
